g.text: PgLoom demo: the classic READ COMMITTED double spend
A wallet service holding $100 receives two concurrent $100 withdrawals.
2 workers · strategy bounded (≤2 preemptions) · max 50 schedules
BEGIN; SELECT balance ...; if balance >= amount { UPDATE ... balance - amount }; COMMIT
: Wallet balance must never drop below zero
Pattern: Unprotected Check-Then-Act under READ COMMITTED
Workers req_a and req_b each read `_pgloom_demo.wallets` without a row lock
and then wrote it in a later statement.
Another transaction committed between the check and the write; READ
COMMITTED re-reads the row for the UPDATE but the application already made
SELECT balance FROM _pgloom_demo.wallets WHERE id = $1 FOR NO KEY UPDATE;
-- FOR NO KEY UPDATE blocks concurrent writers of the row but, unlike FOR UPDATE, not inserts of rows
UPDATE _pgloom_demo.wallets SET balance = balance - $1 WHERE id = $2 AND balance >= $1 RETURNING balance;
-- and verify rows_affected == 1 before reporting success.
Concurrency review for ledgers and payment systems: voskan1989@gmail.com
Act 2: the Fix Advisor's patch applied
SELECT balance FROM wallets WHERE id = $1 FOR NO KEY UPDATE
PASS (all schedules verified, 0 anomalies). The race is fixed.
